derived_from.change: the registry's prefix record on its script made single-process (build/single_process.py) and given a --micro-batch flag (build/gen_failures.py add_micro_batch: default 64, the recorded constant, so the recorded run is the default launch), served exactly, with one synthesised failure: an OOM armed only above the threshold (failures[0])
derived_from.how: the via record's series, steps and timing exactly: the recorded run's first steps

identity.argv_exempt_how: --micro-batch sets the micro-step size only: the global batch is a constant and the loop accumulates over micro-steps, so the optimisation and the step count are the recorded run's at any valid value, and gpu-mock paces per optimizer step. It changes memory, which is what the failure's trigger reads (FAILURE-SERVING.md: the triggering flag in argv_exempt, so the failing launch and its relaunch draw one record)

failures.how: synthesised: no recorded run of this script failed. The sweep file's --micro-batch 256 for this run is a misconfiguration we wrote, and this failure is what an 80 GB card does with it: CUDA out of memory at the first forward, before any optimizer step. At --micro-batch 128 or less the launch is not armed and draws this record clean

If reserved but unallocated memory is large try setting PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True to avoid fragmentation. cause.how: synthesised in PyTorch's OOM wording, as gpu-mock's oversubscription OOM words it (the job modelled as having taken the free card and failing on the remainder): this record's peak scaled to --micro-batch 256, 133.75 GiB, against the daemon's 80 GiB card

threshold.how: the largest micro-batch dividing the global batch's 512 sequences whose peak fits the card (79.19 GiB as torch reports an H100 80GB HBM3, or the daemon's 80 GiB; the same under both). It rests on two assumptions: (1) the base peak, memory.peak = 33.44 GiB at micro-batch 64, provenance inferred: track_1_short/2024-10-10_Muon logs report 34239 MiB peak allocated for the same 12-layer, 768-wide GPT-2 at 64 x 1024 tokens per micro-step on H100; this script does not log memory; (2) that the peak scales linearly in the micro-batch: activations dominate, and weights and optimizer state are about 1.2 GiB, so scaling only the activations gives 65.7 GiB at 128 and 130.1 GiB at 256, the same verdicts. Linear: 66.9 GiB at 128 (fits), 133.7 GiB at 256 (does not)
